clue.text: Replace one weak link with another? Such waste!

definitions.text: Replace one weak link with another?

blocks.clueFragment: Replace one weak link with another?
blocks.note: first meaning: put a fuse, the deliberately weak link in a circuit, back in again
second meaning: rubbish, the noun stressed on the first syllable

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry at a wasteful repair job where a weak link is merely swapped for another one.
explanation.walkthrough: A fuse is the weak link built into a circuit, so replacing it is to re-fuse; the same letters, said differently, are rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Refuse is household rubbish, discarded material thrown away as worthless.

clue.text: In a heap of paper, tramp hides bottle

indicators.note: something that hides another keeps it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a ream is 500 sheets of paper
a hobo is a vagrant

explanation.surface: A vagrant concealing his bottle of drink among a pile of papers.
explanation.walkthrough: The heap of paper does the hiding: it wraps around the tramp.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehoboam is an outsized wine or champagne bottle holding six standard bottles.

clue.text: Spruce and not half trendy, wearing sack

indicators.note: only half the word survives, the rest being dropped
something worn is held by the wearer, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: the first half of the word
to sack is to fire from a job

explanation.surface: Smartened up and only half fashionable, dressed in a hessian sack.
explanation.walkthrough: Spruce looks like the verb for smartening up, but it is the conifer.
explanation.definitionFit: A spruce is a type of conifer, and the Christmas spruce is popularly called by this name.

clue.text: Farmhand, a crock, but able to hold his drink

indicators.note: to hold is to contain, so the first piece wraps round the second

blocks.note: a sherd is a broken piece of pottery, as a crock can be
the drink in question

explanation.surface: A worn-out old farm worker who can nonetheless hold his liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: A crock is both a decrepit person and an earthenware pot or its fragment; sherd is the archaeologist's spelling of shard.
explanation.definitionFit: A swineherd tends pigs, so he is a farm labourer of a particular kind.

clue.text: Produced originally in a hotel! In the Savoy

definitions.text: Produced originally in a hotel! In the Savoy

indicators.note: to produce a show is to put it together and stage it, so these letters are staged in a new order

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: An excited note that some show was first put on in a hotel, namely the Savoy.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: Iolanthe was the first opera premiered at Gilbert and Sullivan's Savoy Theatre, which shares its name with the Savoy Hotel in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera Iolanthe opened at the Savoy Theatre in 1882, so it was produced originally at the Savoy.

clue.text: He was not highly rated, in the main

definitions.text: He was not highly rated, in the main

blocks.clueFragment: He was not highly rated, in the main
blocks.note: surface reading: someone generally thought little of
setter's reading: the main is the sea, and naval ratings are graded, this one at the bottom

explanation.surface: A man who, on the whole, was not thought much of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the main' means mostly but also on the high seas; a rating is a non-commissioned sailor in the Royal Navy.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Royal Navy this was the lowest grade of seaman, below able seaman, so the least highly rated sailor.

clue.text: But most Ancient Greek students get a grounding in this

definitions.text: But most Ancient Greek students get a grounding in this

blocks.clueFragment: But most Ancient Greek students get a grounding in this
blocks.note: surface reading: classical students learn the basics of some subject
setter's reading: the top room of a house is the last place for a grounding, yet the dialect of Athens bears that room's name

explanation.surface: A remark on the basic training that most students of Ancient Greek receive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'But' points to the irony: a grounding sounds like the ground floor, yet the answer is also the room under the roof.
explanation.definitionFit: Attic Greek, the dialect of ancient Athens, is the form taught to most classics students, and an attic is the top storey.

clue.text: Largely restrained artistic medium

indicators.note: largely means most but not all, so the word is cut short

blocks.note: temperate means moderate, held in check

explanation.surface: A painter's materials described as mostly understated.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempera is a paint made by binding pigment with egg yolk, used in medieval panel painting.

clue.text: Put up with being last

blocks.note: first meaning: tolerate
second meaning: continue to exist, as a building may last for centuries

explanation.walkthrough: 'Last' looks like coming at the end, but it is the verb meaning persist.
explanation.definitionFit: To endure is both to bear something unpleasant and to remain in existence over time.

clue.text: So tedious, this work of Mephistopheles?

blocks.note: first meaning: crushingly dull and dispiriting
second meaning, taken literally: the devil's business is the ruin of souls

explanation.surface: A complaint that some task is as tiresome as the devil's own labour.
explanation.walkthrough: Mephistopheles is the devil who bargains for Faust's soul.
explanation.definitionFit: Soul-destroying describes work so monotonous it crushes the spirit, and literally the destruction of souls is the devil's trade.

clue.text: Daring recitation of two poets

indicators.note: a recitation is spoken out loud, so the poets' names count only for how they sound

blocks.note: Thomas Hardy and Thomas Hood, both English poets, spoken one after the other

explanation.surface: A bold performance in which someone recites the work of two poets.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardihood is boldness or audacity, the noun matching daring used as a noun.

clue.text: Inflated stomach — I would apply a compress

blocks.note: tum is an informal word for the stomach
I'd is the contraction of I would
surface padding that completes the medical picture and gives no letters

explanation.surface: Faced with a swollen belly, the speaker would recommend a compress.
explanation.walkthrough: Only 'Inflated stomach — I would' does the work; 'apply a compress' finishes the medical picture and gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tumid describes something swollen or distended, and also bombastic style, so it matches inflated in both senses.

clue.text: Shakespeare had the measure of Dickensian litigant

blocks.note: the Bard is Shakespeare's familiar title
an ell is an old unit of length for cloth

explanation.surface: Shakespeare sizing up a character from Dickens who goes to law.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Bardell is the landlady in The Pickwick Papers who sues Mr Pickwick for breach of promise.
explanation.definitionFit: Mrs Bardell brings the famous breach-of-promise lawsuit in Pickwick, making her a litigant in a Dickens novel.

clue.text: The sort of family that could become critical?

blocks.note: first meaning: the household of two parents and their children
second meaning: describing a reactor or its fuel, which goes critical when the chain reaction sustains itself

explanation.surface: A household whose tensions might tip into crisis at any moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Critical' reads as a family crisis, but in physics it describes a self-sustaining chain reaction.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase for a family of two parents and their children uses this adjective, which also describes reactors that go critical.

clue.text: It's far, yet he heads off for mountain ridge

indicators.note: with their heads off, the words lose their opening letters

blocks.note: the word without its first letter
the word without its first letter
the word without its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone sets off on a long trek though it is far away.
explanation.walkthrough: Behead each of 'far', 'yet' and 'he' and the remainders join as ARETE.
explanation.definitionFit: An arete is a sharp narrow ridge between two glacial valleys, a term borrowed from French by mountaineers.

clue.text: Carer out at work helps run the union

indicators.note: letters at work are busy being rearranged rather than resting in their order

blocks.note: the two words taken as written

explanation.surface: A carer who is away at work helps to organise a trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: The union is the European Union, not a trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: A Eurocrat is an official of the European Union's administration, so one helps run that union.

clue.text: The widow simulated grief for anyone listening

indicators.note: what a listener takes in is sound, so the words are judged by how they are said

blocks.note: a sham is a fake, and pain is grief

explanation.surface: A widow putting on a show of mourning for the benefit of onlookers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Widow is a nickname for Veuve Clicquot, the champagne house named after the widow Clicquot.
explanation.definitionFit: Veuve Clicquot, French for Widow Clicquot, is a famous sparkling wine, so the widow is a nickname for it.

clue.text: People correspond, but not physically

blocks.note: men as people in general
to tally is to match or agree

explanation.surface: Pen friends who write to each other but never meet in person.
explanation.definitionFit: Mentally means in the mind rather than in the body, the opposite of physically.

clue.text: Comes first, able to make runs at speed

indicators.note: the following letters can be made into something new, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sprinter who comes first because they can run fast.
explanation.definitionFit: To predate something is to exist or happen before it, which is to come first in time.

clue.text: Little Kanga having a rest perhaps with Chanticleer

indicators.note: perhaps hints that a different arrangement is possible, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: Roo is Kanga's baby in Winnie-the-Pooh
the word rest reordered

explanation.surface: Kanga's small son taking a nap in the company of a cockerel.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Kanga is not a small kangaroo in general but her child, Roo.
explanation.definitionFit: Chanticleer is the proud cockerel in Chaucer's Nun's Priest's Tale, so a famous example of a male fowl.

clue.text: Man seen at the back of a passage

blocks.note: taken as written
the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A man spotted lurking at the far end of a corridor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the island, not a person; it goes at the back of 'a'.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a walkway between rows of seats, as in a church or theatre, so a passage.

clue.text: Did not punish captured regiment that fought half-heartedly

indicators.note: a captive is held within, so one piece is put inside the other

blocks.note: to spare is to let off punishment
R is an abbreviation for regiment

explanation.surface: A lenient commander who let off a captured regiment that had not fought hard.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to box for practice without full force, so sparred means fought in a restrained way.

clue.text: Talk quietly in, say Ripon church

indicators.note: placed in means put inside what follows

blocks.note: Ripon is a cathedral city and bishopric, an example of a see
p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
CH is the usual abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: An instruction to speak softly in a Yorkshire church.
explanation.walkthrough: Ripon is a small cathedral city in North Yorkshire; 'say' marks it as one example of a bishop's see.
explanation.definitionFit: A speech is a formal talk given to an audience, and talk can be the noun.

clue.text: A little book with one's old qualification

blocks.note: Prov is the short form of Proverbs, a book of the Bible
I for one, plus the 's
O is the standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A slim volume accompanying someone's long-ago certificate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A little book' is a book of the Bible cut short; qualification here means a condition or reservation, not a diploma.
explanation.definitionFit: A proviso is a condition attached to an agreement, a qualification in the sense of a limiting clause.

clue.text: Small detached place that brings in rent?

blocks.note: first meaning: a little island cut off from the land
second meaning, split as ...: a property that ... earns rent

explanation.surface: A small detached house advertised as a source of rental income.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detached' suggests a house; it means separated by water.
explanation.definitionFit: An islet is a very small island, a piece of land standing apart from the shore.

clue.text: Stop snake heading for pitch

blocks.note: an asp is a small venomous snake
to halt is to stop

explanation.surface: A command to halt a snake as it slithers towards a playing field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snake heading for' puts the snake at the head, in front of the stop.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitch is the black tarry substance, and asphalt is the bituminous material of that kind used for roads.

clue.text: Crack up, coming from Essex to London

indicators.note: the letters come out of the words that follow, lying across them

blocks.note: the end of Essex, all of to, and the start of London

explanation.surface: Someone laughing helplessly on the journey from Essex into London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack up' is not laughter here: to crack someone up is to praise them highly.
explanation.definitionFit: To crack up something is to praise it lavishly, as in it is not all it is cracked up to be.

clue.text: Maiden in the river about the end of summer

blocks.note: taken as written
August, abbreviated AUG, is the closing month of summer
the Ural is a river flowing from Russia into the Caspian

explanation.surface: A young woman bathing in a river towards the close of the summer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' here means next to: the river has the month of August beside it. Maiden is the adjective, as in a maiden voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: A maiden speech or voyage is the first one, and inaugural likewise describes something done for the first time.

clue.text: Art gallery threw out a thousand items of historic interest

indicators.note: throwing something out leaves the word without it

blocks.note: the Hermitage in St Petersburg is a great art museum
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A gallery clears out a thousand items from its historic collection.
explanation.definitionFit: Heritage is the collection of buildings, objects and traditions handed down from the past and valued for that history.

clue.text: Dull, but extremely effective

blocks.note: first meaning: deathly boring
second meaning: lethally accurate

explanation.surface: A grudging verdict on something boring that nonetheless works brilliantly.
explanation.definitionFit: Deadly informally means tediously boring, and also means devastatingly accurate or efficient, like a deadly marksman.
